bullets.title: Fed Hawks Signal Rates Need to Stay Higher; AI Inflation Risk Flagged
bullets.body: Fed's Logan said inflation is not on a sustainable path back to 2% without additional policy restriction and that one month of lower CPI data is insufficient—calling for 'modestly higher rates.' Logan also warned AI investment could trigger 'nonlinear price increases' with demand effects already present while productivity benefits lag. Separately, Fed's Schmid characterized inflation as 'persistent across a broad range of goods and services' and pushed back on treating price rises as temporary shocks.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Sector Breaks Below May Highs, Down 5% on the Day
bullets.body: The semiconductor index broke below its initial May highs and is down another 5% on the session, though still up 53% YTD. The Nasdaq gained 0.5%+ while SOX fell 2%+ yesterday—a rare divergence since 2010. MRVL is down 31% and AAOI down 50% this month, with one trader noting 'the entire AI sector is dropping indiscriminately.'

bullets.title: TSM Posts 4th Straight Triple Play, Raises FY Guidance; Stock Drops
bullets.body: TSMC reported Q2 revenue of $39.9B (+25% YoY from $31.9B) and its fourth consecutive quarter beating revenue, operating income, and net income—yet the stock is trading lower. The company raised full-year revenue and capex guidance and printed a 67.7% gross margin. Revenue split: 66% HPC, 22% smartphone, 12% other. Analysts note AI cycle broadening beyond accelerators to full-stack infrastructure.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO Huang: 'We Are at the Beginning of the AI Cycle'; Japan AI Factory Order
bullets.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang declared the AI boom is 'still in its early stages' while visiting Tokyo. Separately, Japan is building what's described as the world's first national AI factory, incorporating 27,500 Nvidia Rubin GPUs, 13,750 Vera CPUs, and 140 MW of data center capacity. Nvidia is characterized as 'the clearest positive public-market read-through' from recent Thinking Machines Inkling model release, which was trained on GB300 NVL72 systems.

bullets.title: GOOGL: EU Orders Android and Search Opened to Rivals; Intel Partnership Inked
bullets.body: The EU has ordered Google to open its Android platform and Search to AI and search rivals under antitrust rules, threatening its competitive moat in Europe. On a more positive note, Intel and Google Cloud expanded their multi-year strategic partnership to deploy Gemini Enterprise and Google Cloud services across Intel's enterprise operations. Google is also renaming NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook and preparing a new personalized avatar feature in the Gemini app.

bullets.title: AAPL: Tens of Millions in Call Flow; OLED iPad Mini Confirmed for 2027
bullets.body: Options flow showed tens of millions in AAPL call sweeps alongside similar GOOGL activity. Apple is confirmed to be readying an OLED iPad Mini alongside low-end and Air updates in 2027. One fintwit trader sold some AAPL 'just now—too good to be true lately,' while another noted Apple may be a beneficiary from the crash in space and semiconductor names.

bullets.title: NFLX Heads Into Q2 Earnings with 4-Straight Post-Report Selloffs
bullets.body: Netflix faces Q2 2026 earnings tonight with investors 'beared up' on engagement headwinds. Over the last four earnings reports, NFLX has declined each time post-announcement, including -9.7% after April earnings and -5.1% a year ago in July.

bullets.title: MU Down 19% Since Burry Short; LTA with QCOM Fails to Arrest Decline
bullets.body: MU announced memory long-term agreements with QCOM but still fell 5.37% on the day. MU is down approximately 19% since Michael Burry went short. One trader questioned whether the decline reflects broader market headwinds rather than company-specific fundamental issues, given the positive LTA news.

bullets.title: AVGO and AAPL: Shift in Semiconductor Pricing Power Signaled
bullets.body: Commentary on X flags that AVGO and AAPL may have signaled a 'major shift in semiconductor pricing power'—Apple's historical leverage over suppliers is eroding as custom silicon complexity grows, while Broadcom gains pricing power from accelerating AI infrastructure demand.

bullets.title: Agentic AI Driving Additive Server-CPU Cycle; Benefits AMD, ARM, INTC
bullets.body: Analysis circulating on fintwit argues agentic AI creates an 'additive server-CPU cycle rather than a pure GPU substitution,' with AMD, ARM, and Intel positioned to benefit from growing inference and processing workloads alongside GPU demand.

bullets.title: Goldman: AI Market Is a 'Rubber Band' With Potential Breaking Points
bullets.body: Goldman traders characterized the AI market as over-extended like a 'rubber band' and flagged potential breaking points in AI valuations. Separately, Goldman slashed its global PC shipment forecast, citing a memory chip crunch derailing the upgrade cycle.

bullets.title: ORCL Down ~50% Since June on OpenAI Exposure Concerns
bullets.body: One fintwit voice noted ORCL is down about 50% since June, framing a short as 'leveraged bearish play on OpenAI exposure' as OpenAI's valuation has risen while Oracle's has collapsed. Separately, chart patterns in ORCL were flagged as resembling those forming in space and chip stocks.

bullets.title: TSLA: Cybercab Revenue Model, Humanoid Lag vs. China Flagged
bullets.body: One analyst modeled Tesla Cybercab at ~$2,500 per unit per quarter pretax profit at scale. Critics on X noted Tesla appears reluctant to showcase its latest humanoid prototypes while Chinese competitors advance rapidly and publicly, questioning Western leadership in humanoids.

bullets.title: LITE and COHR Named by Morgan Stanley as Core CPO Laser Players
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley identified LITE and COHR as core CPO laser players in a recent note, with Fidelity Research and JPMorgan taking active positions. One analyst drew a parallel to LITE's rise from $3B to $60B+ valuation in two years by owning the EML chokepoint, projecting a similar trajectory for SIVE in the CW/CPO market.

bullets.title: Robinhood Chain Breaks Out; Volume Surpasses Established Crypto DEXs
bullets.body: Fundstrat notes Robinhood's Chain product 'quickly turned into a massive breakout pattern' with volume exceeding many established crypto DEXs, according to commentary retweeted by multiple fintwit accounts.

bullets.title: MRVL Sub-THz Wireless Test Validates Data Center Interconnect Roadmap
bullets.body: Marvell-acquired Polariton (acquired April) demonstrated a 226 GHz sub-THz wireless link over 1,400 meters at 153 Gb/s in a Swiss airfield test with ETH Zurich, described as validating Marvell's Data Center Interconnect roadmap.

bullets.title: Macro: Philly Fed Surges to 41.4 (vs. 12.5 Est.); Housing Data Weak
bullets.body: Philadelphia Fed Business Outlook surged to 41.4 in July, the highest since November 2021 and far above the 12.5 consensus, with new orders at +37 and shipments at +33.7. In contrast, pending home sales collapsed 5.4% MoM (vs. -0.5% expected) and the NAHB Housing Market Index fell to 34 vs. 35 estimate. Initial jobless claims beat at 208K vs. 217K expected.

bullets.title: SoftBank/ARM Outlook Upgraded to Stable by S&P on ARM Stock Rise
bullets.body: S&P revised SoftBank Group's outlook from negative to stable, explicitly citing ARM stock appreciation as the key credit-positive factor, while affirming the BB+ rating.

bullets.title: Geopolitical Escalation: U.S.-Iran Strikes, Hormuz Blockade, Dubai Booms
bullets.body: The White House confirmed a full blockade in the Strait of Hormuz and reported the fifth consecutive day of U.S. strikes on Iran, including hits near Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island. Iran warned of 'infrastructure for infrastructure' retaliation and its advisor said damaging Iranian infrastructure could trigger 'total collapse of regional energy supply chain.' Brent crude rallied from ~$70 at start of month to ~$85 before pulling back below $85.

bullets.title: Korea Market Volatility Exceeds GFC Levels; 1-in-30 Retail Investors Margin-Called
bullets.body: Korean stock market volatility is now higher than during both the Global Financial Crisis and the 1990s Asian financial crisis. Goldman reported over 1.2 million leveraged Korean retail accounts triggered margin calls as of July 13, with 320K–360K fully liquidated. Korea has halted new listings of single-stock leveraged ETFs. Goldman is advising clients to rotate from Korea to the 'China AI value chain.'
